title: WCAG 4.5:1 body-text contrast, 3:1 large text, and 7:1 enhanced level
statement:
WCAG requires body text to reach a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background (3:1 for large text) and the stricter enhanced level asks for 7:1, so every text and background pair in a landing page palette, including text over hero images, placeholders and hover or focus text, needs to be checked.

Options:
- AA baseline for body text: Body text at 4.5:1 or higher, for example #767676 on #FFFFFF (about 4.54:1) (fits: professional, balanced, modern)
- Enhanced 7:1 for low-vision and older audiences: Body text at 7:1 or higher (Level AAA), for example #595959 on #FFFFFF (about 7.0:1) or #212121 on #FFFFFF (about 16:1) (fits: clear, trustworthy, clinical)
- Large-text 3:1 latitude: Large display headings (18pt or 14pt bold and above) may use 3:1 (fits: bold, expressive, editorial)
- Scrim under hero text: Text over photos placed on a solid or gradient scrim so the worst-case pixel behind the text still reaches 4.5:1 (fits: premium, photographic, cinematic)
- States and placeholders: Placeholder text and text revealed on hover or keyboard focus held to 4.5:1 as well (fits: polished, accessible, careful)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general, seniors.

source.title: Understanding SC 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum), Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
source.venue: W3C WCAG 2.2 (SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA; SC 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced), Level AAA)
